docs.title: GitHub API Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the beginner-friendly GitHub API documentation project. This guide introduces key concepts such as users, repositories, issues, and authentication, using simple explanations and code examples.

Note: This project was created using Markdown and MkDocs Material to demonstrate how to write and publish developer-friendly documentation.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Many API documentations assume a lot of background knowledge. This project aims to explain the GitHub API from a newcomer’s perspective, breaking down the basics of how it works.

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:
• Users
  • Repositories
  • Issues
  • Authentication

Each topic includes a brief explanation and code examples using curl to demonstrate how to make API requests.

This project was created as part of a technical writing portfolio and is not affiliated with GitHub Inc.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
To access GitHub's API, you typically need to authenticate using a personal access token.

Example:

curl -H "Authorization: token YOUR_TOKEN" https://api.github.com/user
  • Authentication is required for most write operations and some read operations.
  • A token is like a password and should be kept secret.

docs.title: Issues
docs.text:
Issues are used to track tasks, enhancements, and bugs.

Example:

curl https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/issues
  • You can create issues, comment on them, and close them using the API.
  • Each issue has a title, description, and can be labeled or assigned.

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
A repository (or "repo") is a project container that holds files, issues, pull requests, and more.

Example:

curl https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World
  • Repos can be public or private.
  • You can list, create, update, and delete repositories through the API.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
GitHub users are individual accounts that can own repositories and collaborate on projects.

Example:

curl https://api.github.com/users/octocat
  • A user can follow others, create repositories, and star projects.
  • Each user has a public profile that can be accessed via the API.
